### Observed differences

- In the later window, A19 and A20 appear in far more traces: A19 in about 48 in 100 traces (about 24 before) and A20 in about 53 in 100 (about 21 before), in each case occurring at most once per trace in nearly all cases. [OCC001, OCC002]
- A19 and A20 remain almost mutually exclusive: they occur together in only about 2 in 100 later traces (none before), and in the later window nearly every trace contains exactly one of them, whereas before about 55 in 100 traces contained neither. [REL001]
- A23 participates less often: about 42 in 100 later traces versus about 56 in 100 before. [OCC003]
- The outgoing transitions of A40 are redistributed: before, about 46 in 100 went to A25, with about 18 to A19 and about 17 to A20; in the later window about 47 in 100 go to A20 and about 41 to A19, and a direct A40 → A25 transition is not observed among the roughly 203 outgoing transitions. [DIR001]
- A19 and A20 now sit between A40 and A25 in the execution order: A40 precedes A19 in about 48 in 100 later traces (about 24 before) and A19 precedes A25 in about 47 in 100 (about 23 before); likewise A40 precedes A20 in about 52 in 100 (about 21 before) and A20 precedes A25 in about 53 in 100 (about 21 before). [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]
- The positional gap from A40 to A25 widens by about one step: a distance of 1 step falls from about 47 in 100 to none, while a distance of 2 steps rises to about 86 in 100 (about 44 before). [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, executions route from A40 to A25 via A19 or A20 — split roughly evenly between the two, which almost never both occur — in place of the direct A40 → A25 transition seen before, with A23 also appearing in fewer traces. This rests on direct relational and positional evidence: the successor profile of A40 shifted from mostly A25 to mostly A19 and A20, A40 consistently precedes and A19/A20 consistently precede A25 in about half of the later traces, and the A40 → A25 step distance moved from 1–2 to 2–3, consistent with one intermediate activity. [DIR001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, LAG001]

The nine items far exceed the roughly 0.5 expected by chance at these thresholds, and the participation, routing and ordering items all describe one coherent rerouting rather than independent phenomena. Limitations: the direct A40 → A25 transition being unobserved in the later window shows only that it did not occur among the roughly 203 sampled outgoing transitions, not that the edge is gone; a sampling-driven shift in the mix of pre-existing variants could contribute to the participation changes, although a fall from about 46 in 100 transitions to none is hard to explain by sampling alone; and no relational item connects A23 to the rerouting, so the reason for its lower participation remains open. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL001, DIR001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

We have two windows of 200 traces each. Screening: 103 units tested, 0.51 items expected without change. We have 9 evidence items. That's many times larger than 0.51 (about 18x), so the count cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we move past the "insufficient evidence by count" gate.

Now let's understand the items:

OCC001: A19 participation increased from 0.235 (about 47/200) to 0.485 (about 97/200). Mean occurrences per trace also 0.235 → 0.485, recurrence 0. So A19 appears at most once per trace, but in more traces.

OCC002: A20 participation increased from 0.215 (43/200) to 0.53 (106/200). Mean occurrences 0.215 → 0.535, recurrence 0.005. So A20 also appears more often, occasionally repeated.

OCC003: A23 participation decreased from 0.555 (111/200) to 0.42 (84/200). Mean occurrences 0.565 → 0.42.

DIR001: outgoing transitions of A40 redistributed. Before: A25 46%, A19 18%, A20 17%, A08 6.5%, A04 3.5%, A06 3%, A10 3%, A02 1.5%, A09 0.5%, A30 0.5%. After: A20 47%, A19 41%, A10 2.5%, A08 3%, A06 2%, A02 2%, others small. Notably A25 → 0 in after (A25 no longer observed as a target of A40), while A19 and A20 dominate. Support: 201 outgoing transitions before, 203 after.

REL001: A19 & A20 pair. Before: neither 55%, A_only 23.5%, B_only 21.5%, cooccurrence 0. After: neither 0%, A_only 47%, B_only 51.5%, cooccurrence 1.5%. So before, A19 and A20 almost never appeared in the same trace; after, they still rarely co-occur (1.5%) but nearly every trace contains at least one of them. Interesting: they are alternatives — when one appears the other doesn't. Actually A_only 47% + B_only 51.5% + cooccurrence 1.5% = 100%. So after, every trace has exactly one of A19 or A20 (mostly). Before, 55% of traces had neither.

REL002: A19 & A25. Before: B_only (A25 only) 76.5%, cooccurrence 23.5%, A_before_B 22.5%. After: cooccurrence 48.5%, B_only 51.5%, A_before_B 47%. So A19 now co-occurs with A25 in about 48.5 in 100 traces (up from 23.5), and A19 before A25 in 47% (up from 22.5%).

REL003: A19 & A40. Before: B_only (A40 only) 76.5%, cooccurrence 23.5%, B_before_A 23.5%. After: cooccurrence 48.5%, B_only 51.5%, B_before_A 47.5%. So A40 before A19 in 47.5% (up from 23.5%).

REL004: A20 & A25. Before: B_only 78.5%, cooccurrence 21.5%, A_before_B 21%. After: cooccurrence 53%, B_only 47%, A_before_B 52.5%. So A20 before A25 in 52.5% (up from 21%).

REL005: A20 & A40. Before: B_only 78.5%, cooccurrence 21.5%, B_before_A 21%. After: cooccurrence 53%, B_only 47%, B_before_A 52%. So A40 before A20 in 52% (up from 21%).

LAG001: A40 → A25 distance. Before: distance 1 in 46.5%, distance 2 in 43.5%, distance 3 in 9.5%, distance 4 in 0.5%. After: distance 2 in 86%, distance 3 in 13%, distance 1 in 0%. So the gap between A40 and A25 shifted from mostly 1–2 steps to mostly 2–3 steps.

Now, what's the underlying story? Let me try to reconstruct.

Before: A19 in 23.5% traces, A20 in 21.5%, A23 in 55.5%. A19 and A20 never co-occur (cooccurrence 0 before). A40 occurs in essentially all traces (support 201 outgoing transitions over 200 traces — so A40 appears in ~all traces, possibly some repeats). A40 → A25 in 46% of A40's outgoing transitions before; after, A40 → A19 41% and A40 → A20 47%, A40 → A25 0%.

REL002/REL003: A19 co-occurs with A25 in 23.5% before — that matches A19's participation 23.5%. So whenever A19 appears, it co-occurs with A25, and A19 before A25 in 22.5% (nearly always when co-occurring). Similarly A40 before A19 in 23.5% — so the pattern before is A40 → A19 → A25 in ~23.5% of traces. Similarly for A20: A20 co-occurs with A25 21.5%, A20 before A25 21%, A40 before A20 21%. So before: A40 → A20 → A25 in ~21% of traces. And A40 → A25 directly in 46% of outgoing transitions.

Hmm wait, before A40's outgoing: A25 46%, A19 18%, A20 17%. So in ~18% of A40 occurrences, next relevant activity is A19; ~17% A20; ~46% A25. The A19/A20 paths then lead to A25 (A19 before A25 22.5% of traces; A20 before A25 21%).

After: A19 in 48.5%, A20 in 53%, A23 in 42%. A19 and A20 still rarely co-occur (1.5%) — they're mutually exclusive alternatives. A40 → A19 41%, A40 → A20 47%, A40 → A25 0%. A19 before A25 47%, A40 before A19 47.5%; A20 before A25 52.5%, A40 before A20 52%. LAG: A40 → A25 distance now 2–3 steps instead of 1–2.

So the story: after the change, A40 is followed by A19 or A20 (roughly half each), which is then followed by A25; the direct A40 → A25 transition disappeared. Before, A40 → A25 directly in ~46% of cases, and via A19 or A20 in ~35% of cases (18% + 17%). Also A23 participation dropped from 55.5% to 42%.

Hmm, but wait — the hypothesis isn't given to us. The task says "judge whether they support a hypothesis about a structural change in the process." Actually the prompt says: "compare evidence ... and judge whether they support a hypothesis about a structural change in the process." There's no explicit hypothesis stated in the input. So we formulate our own inference: the evidence supports a structural change — specifically, a rerouting around A40: the direct A40 → A25 transition was replaced by A40 → A19/A20 → A25, with A19 and A20 now appearing in about half the traces each as mutually exclusive alternatives, and the A40→A25 gap widening by one step. Also A23 participates less.

Let me check consistency:

- OCC001, OCC002: A19 and A20 participation roughly doubled (23.5% → 48.5%; 21.5% → 53%).
- OCC003: A23 decreased (55.5% → 42%).
- DIR001: A40's outgoing redistributed: A25 share dropped from 46% to 0%; A19 rose to 41%, A20 to 47%.
- REL001: A19 and A20 remain (nearly) mutually exclusive; before 55% of traces had neither, after ~0%.
- REL002–REL005: A19/A20 now co-occur with A25 in ~half the traces and consistently precede A25; A40 precedes A19/A20 in ~half.
- LAG001: A40 → A25 distance shifted from 1–2 to 2–3 steps, consistent with an intermediate activity (A19 or A20) inserted between them.

This is a coherent, direct story: an insertion/rerouting between A40 and A25. The relational evidence (REL002–005) and lag evidence (LAG001) directly support the placement change. The DIR evidence shows the successor change directly.

Competing explanations: sampling differences in variant frequencies — a rare variant appearing in one window only. Could the after-window just have more of a rare variant that includes A19/A20 between A40 and A25? Before, A40→A19 was 18% and A40→A20 17% — these aren't rare. The shift from 46% direct to 0% direct is large. With 200 traces per window and ~200 A40 outgoing transitions each, a drop from 46% to 0% (about 93 transitions to 0) is very unlikely under random splitting. But formally, the competing explanation is that variant frequencies shifted due to sampling — e.g., the process has two variants and the mix shifted. Actually a mix shift is itself a behavioural change... The instruction says mention sampling differences in variant frequencies where relevant.

Also, "zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window" — A25 as a target of A40 has zero share after; we should say A40 → A25 was not observed in the later window, not that the edge was removed.

Now the count check: 9 items vs 0.51 expected — many times larger (about 18×). So we proceed. All items have empirical_strength 0.995 (i.e., larger than all 199/200 reference differences). The items are consistent and mutually reinforcing, but note: several indicators reflect the same trace behaviour (OCC001/REL001/REL002/REL003 all involve A19; OCC002/REL004/REL005 involve A20). They aren't independent confirmations, but they do describe one coherent underlying difference from multiple angles, which is what we want for directness and consistency.

Support level: Supported hypothesis. The evidence directly shows: successor redistribution at A40 (DIR001), positional/relational insertion of A19/A20 between A40 and A25 (REL002–005, LAG001), and participation changes (OCC001–003). This is direct relational/positional evidence for a placement/routing change. The hypothesis: in the later window, traces route from A40 to A25 via A19 or A20 (roughly equal split, mutually exclusive), whereas before, A40 frequently led directly to A25; A23 participates less.

Limitations: finite samples; the disappearance of the direct A40→A25 edge means only that it was not observed in the later window (203 outgoing transitions); sampling variation in variant mix could contribute; A23's decrease is not explained by the rerouting evidence (no relational item involving A23), so its role is unclear.

Wait — should I be careful about whether the hypothesis is "supported" vs "weak"? Criteria: "Supported hypothesis: the evidence supports a specific hypothesis directly and consistently." We have direct relational evidence (REL, LAG, DIR successor changes) showing the rerouting. The count is many times the chance expectation. Consistency: all items align with one story. Competing explanations: sampling — but the magnitude (46% → 0% on ~200 transitions; participation doubling on ~90+ traces) makes pure sampling unlikely, though we can't fully rule out a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants (i.e., the process always had both variants and the after window sampled more of the A19/A20 variant). Hmm — actually that's a real competing explanation: if the process is a mixture of variants and the windows sampled different mixes, we'd see exactly this. But is a mix shift a "structural change"? The instruction says don't assume a structural change exists; "insufficient evidence" is valid. But here the difference is large and consistent across many indicators. The guidance: "A count many times larger cannot be explained by chance as a whole, even when all items describe one underlying difference." So 9 items vs 0.51 → proceed to qualitative judgement.

For a placement hypothesis we need relational/positional evidence showing the change directly — we have it: REL002–005 show A19/A20 now precede A25 and follow A40 in ~half the traces (before ~21–24%), LAG001 shows the A40→A25 gap shifting from 1–2 to 2–3 steps, DIR001 shows A40's successors shifting from mostly A25 to A19/A20. That's direct.

So it's not a new activity; it's that the routing shifted: the direct A40→A25 path became unobserved, and the via-A19/A20 path became the dominant one, with A19/A20 frequency roughly doubling. So the hypothesis: rerouting between A40 and A25 — the direct transition from A40 to A25 was replaced by paths through A19 or A20 (mutually exclusive alternatives), and A23 participates less often.

The 46% A25 share + 18% A19 + 17% A20 = 81%; the rest ~19% goes to A08, A04, A06, A10, A02, A09, A30. Those intermediate activities then presumably lead to A25 eventually. Fine — I don't need to fully reconstruct.)

LAG001: A40 → A25 within five steps: before distance 1 (46.5%), 2 (43.5%), 3 (9.5%), 4 (0.5%). After: 2 (86%), 3 (13%). So the direct adjacency (distance 1) disappeared; the gap is now 2–3 steps, consistent with one intermediate activity (A19 or A20) inserted. Good.

So the behavioural description:

- A19 and A20 appear in far more traces in the later window: A19 in about 48 in 100 traces vs 24 before; A20 in about 53 in 100 vs 22 before. Both at most once per trace (recurrence ~0).
- A19 and A20 remain (almost) mutually exclusive: they co-occur in only about 2 in 100 later traces (0 before); in the later window essentially every trace contains exactly one of them, whereas before 55 in 100 contained neither.
- A23 participation fell from about 56 in 100 to 42 in 100.
- A40's outgoing transitions redistributed: before, the largest share went to A25 (about 46 in 100), with A19 (18) and A20 (17) next; in the later window, A19 (41) and A20 (47) dominate and A40 → A25 was not observed.
- A19 and A20 now sit between A40 and A25: A40 before A19 in ~48 in 100 (vs 24), A19 before A25 in ~47 (vs 23); similarly A40 before A20 ~52 (vs 21), A20 before A25 ~53 (vs 21). A25 co-occurs with A19/A20 in about half of traces (up from ~22–24).
- The positional gap from A40 to A25 shifted from mostly 1–2 steps to 2–3 steps (distance 1: 47% → 0%; distance 2: 44% → 86%).

Inference: Supported hypothesis — in the later window, executions appear to route from A40 to A25 through A19 or A20 (roughly an even split between the two, rarely both), instead of the previously observed direct A40 → A25 transition; A23 participates less often. Supporting signs: direct successor redistribution at A40, consistent relational ordering (A40 before A19/A20 before A25), and the widened A40→A25 distance; the number of items (9) is far above the ~0.5 expected by chance. Limitations: the direct A40→A25 edge being unobserved in the later window doesn't prove removal (203 outgoing transitions observed); sampling differences in variant mix could produce some of the shift, though the size (46% → 0% of ~200 transitions) makes pure sampling unlikely; A23's decline isn't connected to the rerouting by any relational item, so its role in the change is unclear.
